name: Frame Rate Lifter
purpose: Convert a 30 fps film to 60 fps or higher. audit checks a studio project before a native re-render (30 fps video layers, moves that still strobe at the target rate from qa/motion/tweens.json, stepped motion, fps lookups, page motion blur) and --apply sets project.json fps. analyse and convert interpolate any finished film per frame pair (copy, blend or FFmpeg minterpolate) from a leave-one-out probe, then verify and sheet check the result.
capabilities: doctor | audit [--apply] | analyse | convert | verify | sheet
leave-one-out probe: every other frame rebuilt with each method and scored against the real frame (mean + worst-block error)
cut, hold, stepped-cadence and dissolve detection; per-pair plan stored as compact strings in a JSON plan with segments and review moments
streaming stitcher on raw yuv420p pipes: integer-phase frames are source frames, audio copied, output written to .partial and renamed on success
verify: frame count, duration, audio, size and distinct frames per second (a duplicate-padded 60 fps film reads about 30)
src/pipeline/framerate.py holds the pure planning, stitching, GSAP ease-slope and tween-audit logic

installation.instructions: Workspace file; needs ffmpeg/ffprobe with minterpolate and numpy (Pillow for sheet).

compatibility.notes: Tested on Windows with FFmpeg 9.0.2: a 24 s 720x1280 film converted to 60 fps in 408 s (minterpolate is single-threaded, about 3.6 output frames/s), probe 29.6 s. Memory stays at a few frames. Not yet run on the M2.

licensing.notes: Internal workspace component; no third-party code copied. Calls the host FFmpeg.

security.notes: Runs local ffmpeg/ffprobe; the probe takes the host analysis lock and conversion the render lock (src/pipeline/hostlock.py). Writes only to the output film, its plan and qa/frame-rate/; audit --apply edits project.json fps and runs studio.py formats.

approval_evidence: tests/test-frame-rate.py (23 tests, including a synthetic 60 fps ground-truth round trip where auto beat frame doubling 4.3x on a slide and 3.1x on a dissolve); sample-engine-mix lifted to 60 fps on 2026-11-25 (52.7 vs 28.3 distinct frames/s, full-resolution crops inspected). Experimental until it has run on the render host.
